slides.title: Public Key Infrastructure (PKI)
points: PKI uses asymmetric cryptography, certificates, and trust relationships to help systems verify identities and protect communications.
Security+ Objective 1.4: explain the importance of using appropriate cryptographic solutions.

slides.title: Public Key
slides.teach: The shareable half of an asymmetric key pair.

course.learn: The shareable half of an asymmetric key pair.

breakdown.explanation: It can be distributed openly and is used for encryption or signature verification depending on the operation.
Encrypt data for the key owner, Verify a digital signature

course.why: It enables others to securely interact with the key owner without exposing the private key.
course.example: A server publishes a certificate containing its public key.
course.check_q: Which half of an asymmetric key pair may be distributed openly?

slides.title: Private Key
slides.teach: The secret half of an asymmetric key pair.

course.learn: The secret half of an asymmetric key pair.

breakdown.explanation: It must remain protected and is used for decryption or signing depending on the operation.
Decrypt data encrypted to the public key, Create a digital signature

course.why: Anyone who gains the private key may be able to impersonate the owner or decrypt protected data.
course.example: A web server stores its private key securely and never sends it to clients.
course.check_q: Which key should never be distributed to clients?

slides.title: Key Escrow
slides.teach: A controlled process where a copy of a cryptographic key is stored for authorized recovery.

course.learn: A controlled process where a copy of a cryptographic key is stored for authorized recovery.

breakdown.explanation: It is a recoverable backup of a key under defined controls.

course.why: It can prevent permanent loss of access to encrypted business data.
course.example: An organization can recover encrypted files after the employee who owned the key leaves.
course.check_q: What concept stores a recoverable copy of a cryptographic key?

cards.name: Key Escrow

blocks.title: Public, private, or recoverable?
items: The public key can be distributed without revealing the private key.
Example: A server publishes its certificate containing its public key.
The private key must remain protected because it proves control of the key pair.
Example: A server never sends its private key to clients.
Escrow stores a recoverable copy of a key under controlled access.
Example: An organization recovers encrypted data after an employee leaves.
blocks.example: Memory: Public = share · Private = secret · Escrow = recover.

questions.q: A web server publishes a certificate so clients can obtain a key used to verify its digital signatures. Which key is being shared?
questions.explanation: The public key can be distributed and used to verify signatures created with the corresponding private key.

questions.q: Which key must remain secret because compromise could allow impersonation of the owner?
questions.explanation: The private key must remain protected.

questions.q: An organization stores recoverable copies of encryption keys under strict administrative control. Which concept is this?
questions.explanation: Key escrow provides controlled recovery of cryptographic keys.

questions.q: A user encrypts data using a recipient's shareable key so only the recipient can decrypt it with the corresponding secret key. Which key did the user use?
questions.explanation: In asymmetric encryption, the recipient's public key is used to encrypt data for that recipient.

questions.q: A company wants to ensure encrypted business records remain recoverable if an employee loses access to a key. Which solution best addresses this requirement?
questions.explanation: Key escrow allows authorized recovery of a stored key.
